request.description: Business-only. One row per paid-or-attempted booking (payment must exist). keyword searches service name, customer name/email, Stripe transaction id, and amount. status filters on the friendly payment label (paid/pending/refunded/failed), not the raw Payment.status enum. startDate/endDate filter on the booking date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Each row includes target { id, name, price, actaulPrice, preferredServiceType } (same shape as the booking own target subdocument -- serviceName was dropped in favor of target.name), transactionId (Stripe PaymentIntent id), and amount (captured Payment.amount, falling back to the target price). meta.statusCounts = { all, paid, pending, refunded, failed } -- tab badge counts, computed from every filter except the status tab itself (so counts stay stable while switching tabs), for the All/Paid/Pending/Refunded/Failed filter chips.

Business-only receipt/detail view for a single billing-history row (a booking with a payment). Trimmed to receipt fields: businessName, target { id, name, price, actaulPrice, preferredServiceType } (same shape as the booking own target subdocument -- serviceName/serviceType dropped as redundant with target.name/target.preferredServiceType), slot, sessionSlotMins, customerName, paymentStatus, paymentMethod, transactionId, price, currency, platformPayment (our application fee, major units). 403s if the booking does not belong to the caller business.

request.description: Works for both user and business tokens — scoped to whichever the caller is (req.user.userType). Returns a lean projection for calendar cells: _id, bookingId, scope, slot, date, status, userInfo, businessInfo, name, photos. meta.statuses is the unfiltered status-count breakdown for the date range (ignores the status query param).

Also returns transactionId (Stripe PaymentIntent id), platformFeeAmount (our application fee, major units), and paymentStatusLabel (paid/pending/refunded/failed) -- useful for a billing receipt/detail screen.

Time-based fork: slot <= 4 days away -> PaymentIntent auth hold (intentType 'payment'); > 4 days -> SetupIntent card vaulting (intentType 'setup'). stripePaymentMethodId is REQUIRED (client-side createPaymentMethod(), not a hardcoded pm_card_visa shortcut) — no Booking, not even a checkout draft, is created without it. Response is either { booking, intentType } (payment confirmed immediately, no 3DS needed) or { draftId, clientSecret, intentType } (3DS required — complete with handleNextAction/handleNextActionForSetup(clientSecret); the real Booking only gets created once the Stripe webhook confirms it, not from this response).

request.description: Business marks the service completed. Captures the Stripe authorization hold (platform fee split in prod). If capture fails the customer is debt-locked until they settle.

Insufficient-funds recovery for requires_payment_fix bookings. stripePaymentMethodId is optional: omit it to retry the card already vaulted on the booking (on-session — a required 3DS challenge comes back as { clientSecret, intentType: 'payment' } instead of hard-declining); supply a fresh pm_ id to vault a new card and retry with it instead ({ clientSecret, intentType: 'setup' } if the vault itself needs 3DS; once vaulted, a second { clientSecret, intentType: 'payment' } is possible if the retry charge also needs its own challenge). 400 booking_payment_method_required if no card is on file at all; 400 booking_payment_fix_failed if the card (existing or new) is declined outright.

request.description: Business self-service Analytics screen (business role). range: 7d|30d|90d, defaults to 90d. Returns profileViews, searchAppearances, bookingRequests, conversions, avgRating, revenue -- each as { count/average/amountMinor, changePercent } vs the immediately-preceding period of the same length -- plus performanceChart (all-time monthly revenue, same series as home.stats.performanceChart). profileViews/searchAppearances are now tracked via a new BusinessAnalyticsEvent collection: a profile_view is logged on every GET /app/businesses/:businessId/overview hit (customer-only route), a search_impression is logged for every business returned by GET /app/users/businesses (only when the caller is a customer). conversions = bookings created in the period whose status moved past "requested" (i.e. the business accepted them) -- an approximation, since there is no view/search-to-booking attribution.

Revenue screen (business role). availableToWithdraw / pendingPayout come from the live Stripe Connect balance (same source as home.stats.withdrawable). grossRevenue/netEarned are for the last full calendar month with changePercent vs the month before that (netEarned assumes the flat 5% platform fee, same rate as APPLICATION_FEE_PERCENT). perClient is a 5-row preview of GET /app/bookings/billing-history?status=paid -- "See All" on this screen should just deep-link to that existing endpoint/screen.

Updates the caller's own review, identified by its _id in the path. The review is looked up by { _id: reviewId, subject: <authenticated user> } — 404 review_not_found if this user isn't the one who left that review, so only the original reviewer can ever update it. rating accepts a decimal between 1 and 5 (e.g. 4.5), not just whole numbers.
'Complete Payment' button: settles the failed capture (debt lock), clears hasOutstandingDebt, marks the booking captured/completed.

Manage Card screen -- add a new saved card (customer role). IMPORTANT: paymentMethodId must be a Stripe PaymentMethod id (pm_xxx) created client-side via Stripe.js/the mobile SDK (createPaymentMethod) -- raw card number/CVC must NEVER be sent to this API directly (PCI/Stripe ToS). cardHolderName (optional) is saved both on our own Card collection and pushed to the Stripe PaymentMethod billing_details.name. Creates the caller Stripe Customer on the first card if one does not exist yet. setDefault (optional) makes it the default card for future charges. Response data._id is our own Card document id (use this, not the Stripe pm_xxx, for the update/delete endpoints below).

List the caller saved cards (customer role) -- backed by our own Card collection (scoped strictly to req.user._id), not a live Stripe Customer lookup. Each item: { _id (our Card document id -- use this for update/delete, not a Stripe id), brand, last4, expMonth, expYear, cardHolderName, isDefault }.

Update a saved card (customer role). :cardId is our own Card document _id (from GET /cards), NOT the Stripe pm_xxx. All body fields optional: cardHolderName, expMonth, expYear, isDefault. Ownership is checked against our own Card collection (Card.findOne({ _id: cardId, user })), independent of Stripe Customer sync. Stripe never allows changing a card own number or CVC on an existing PaymentMethod (PCI scope) -- only billing_details.name and the expiry can be updated; to change the actual card number the customer must add a new card instead. 404s card_not_found if the Card doc was not added by the caller.

Detach/remove a saved card (customer role). :cardId is our own Card document _id (from GET /cards), NOT the Stripe pm_xxx. Ownership is checked against our own Card collection. 404s card_not_found if the Card doc was not added by the caller.

Withdraw Funds screen -- lists the business Stripe Connect payout destinations (bank accounts and debit cards). Each item: { id, type: "bank_account"|"card", bankName, brand, last4, isDefault }. 400 stripe_onboarding_required if the business has no Stripe Connect account yet.

Confirm Withdrawal button on the Withdraw Funds screen. amount is in major units (dollars); payoutMethodId is the id of a payout method from GET .../payout-methods. Triggers a REAL Stripe payout (stripe.payouts.create) on the business Connect account for that amount -- 400s with insufficient_withdrawable_balance if amount exceeds the live available balance, or invalid_withdrawal_amount if amount is not a positive number. The connected account payout schedule is set to "manual" (at account creation, and lazily via ensureManualPayoutSchedule for older accounts) so Stripe never also auto-pays out the same balance on its own rolling schedule. Funds arrive in 2-3 business days via Stripe Connect.

request.description:
### Send Email

This endpoint allows you to send an email to the specified recipients.

#### Request Body

- title (string, optional): The title of the email.
    
- emails (array of strings): The list of email addresses to which the email will be sent.
    
- subject (string, required): The subject of the email.
    
- body (string, required): The body content of the email.
    
- config (object):
    
    - fromEmail (string, required): The sender's email address.
        
    - isHtml (boolean, required): Indicates whether the email body is in HTML format.

The response is in JSON format with the following schema:

``` json

  "type": "object",
 ```

request.description:
Paginated badge list for the admin panel. Admin only (401 without a token, 403 for any other role).

Separate from GET {{url}}badges, which is the app-facing list and differs in two ways:
  - it never paginates (the apps build their profile forms from it and need every badge in one response)
  - its ?scope folds both-badges into each audience, so ?scope=business returns business AND both badges

meta carries:
  - currentPage / totalPages / totalRecords / limit
  - scopeList — counts per tab: { all, user, business, both }. Because scope is matched exactly the buckets are disjoint, so user + business + both === all. Counted from the current filter minus scope, so choosing a tab does not move the tab numbers, while keyword/status narrow all of them together.
  - scopeTypeList / statusTypeList — the allowed filter values.
